```ts
const OPENROUTER_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions";

export interface ToolCall {
  id: string;
  type: "function";
  function: { name: string; arguments: string };
}

export interface ChatMessage {
  role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool";
  content: string | null;
  tool_calls?: ToolCall[];
  tool_call_id?: string;
}

export interface ToolDefinition {
  type: "function";
  function: {
    name: string;
    description: string;
    parameters: Record<string, unknown>;
  };
}

export async function createChatCompletion(
  messages: ChatMessage[],
  tools?: ToolDefinition[]
): Promise<ChatMessage> {
  const apiKey = process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    throw new Error("OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set");
  }

  const response = await fetch(OPENROUTER_URL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: process.env.OPENROUTER_MODEL || "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5",
      messages,
      ...(tools ? { tools } : {}),
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const body = await response.text();
    throw new Error(`OpenRouter request failed (${response.status}): ${body}`);
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { choices?: { message?: ChatMessage }[] };
  const message = data.choices?.[0]?.message;

  if (!message) {
    throw new Error("OpenRouter response did not include a message");
  }

  return message;
}
```

Key facts:
- `createChatCompletion(messages: ChatMessage[], tools?: ToolDefinition[]): Promise<ChatMessage>` â€” `tools` is optional, so it's directly reusable for a tool-free title-generation call (just omit the second argument).
- No config module wraps this â€” API key (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) and model (`OPENROUTER_MODEL`, default `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"`) are read directly from `process.env` inline in this function. There's no separate model constant/param for a "cheaper/faster" title model â€” you'd need to either add an optional model parameter to `createChatCompletion` or hardcode/env-configure a second model name for titles.
- `ChatMessage.content` is typed `string | null` (assistant tool-call-only messages have null content).

```tsx
  const bottomRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const textareaRef = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    api
      .getConversation(conversationId)
      .then(setConversation)
      .catch((err) => {
        if (err instanceof ApiError && err.status === 404) {
          setNotFound(true);
        } else {
          setLoadError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
        }
      });
  }, [conversationId]);

  useEffect(() => {
    bottomRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" });
  }, [conversation?.messages.length]);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Wait for the re-render that clears `disabled` before focusing â€” a
    // disabled textarea silently refuses focus().
    if (!sending) textareaRef.current?.focus();
  }, [sending]);

  const sendContent = async (content: string, tempId: number) => {
    if (!conversation) return;
    setSending(true);

    try {
      const assistantMessage = await api.sendMessage(conversation.id, content);
      setConversation((prev) => {
        if (!prev) return prev;
        const messages = prev.messages.map((m) => (m.id === tempId ? { ...m, status: undefined } : m));
        return { ...prev, messages: [...messages, assistantMessage] };
      });
      setTripRefreshSignal((n) => n + 1);
    } catch {
```

### 5.4 `client/src/Layout.tsx` (full rewrite)

```ts

}

const SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED_KEY = "sidebarCollapsed";
const MOBILE_QUERY = "(max-width: 700px)";

export function Layout(): JSX.Element
```

State:
- `isMobile = useMediaQuery(MOBILE_QUERY)`
- `mobileOpen: boolean` (drawer open/closed, default `false`)
- `desktopCollapsed: boolean`, lazily initialized from `localStorage.getItem(SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED_KEY) === "1"` (wrapped in try/catch for SSR/privacy-mode safety), persisted via a `useEffect` on change.

Logic:
```ts

  if (isMobile) setMobileOpen((v) => !v);
  else setDesktopCollapsed((v) => !v);
};
const sidebarHidden = isMobile ? !mobileOpen : desktopCollapsed;
```
One button, one handler â€” `matchMedia` (via `isMobile`) decides which state it actually flips, so there's no cross-contamination between the two independent booleans.

Render tree:
```tsx

  <div className={`app-shell${desktopCollapsed ? " sidebar-collapsed" : ""}`}>
    {isMobile && mobileOpen && <div className="drawer-backdrop" onClick={() => setMobileOpen(false)} />}
    <Sidebar
      mobileOpen={mobileOpen}
      hidden={sidebarHidden}
      onCloseMobile={() => setMobileOpen(false)}
      closeButtonRef={closeButtonRef}
    />
    <div className="content-column">
      <TopBar title={topBarTitle} onToggleSidebar={toggleSidebar} toggleButtonRef={toggleButtonRef} />
      <main className="app-main">

  </div>
</ConversationsProvider>
```

`Sidebar` is **always mounted** (never conditionally rendered) â€” only its CSS width/transform and `inert` attribute change â€” so the collapse/expand and drawer slide are pure CSS transitions, not mount/unmount churn.

```ts
export async function getExchangeRate(from: string, to: string, amount = 1) {
  const fromCode = from.toUpperCase();
  const toCode = to.toUpperCase();

  const url = new URL("https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/latest");
  url.searchParams.set("base", fromCode);
  url.searchParams.set("symbols", toCode);

  const response = await fetch(url);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Exchange rate lookup failed (${response.status})`);
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as FrankfurterResponse;
  const rate = data.rates[toCode];
  if (rate === undefined) {
    throw new Error(`No exchange rate found for ${fromCode} to ${toCode}`);
  }

  return {
    from: fromCode,
    to: toCode,
    amount,
    converted: Number((rate * amount).toFixed(4)),
    rate,
    date: data.date,
  };
}
```

```ts
async function geocodeLocation(query: string): Promise<GeocodeResult> {
  const url = new URL("https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search");
  url.searchParams.set("name", query);

  const data = (await response.json()) as { results?: GeocodeResult[] };

  if (!result) {
    throw new Error(`Could not find a location matching "${query}"`);
  }
  return result;
}

export async function getCurrentWeather(location: string) {
  const place = await geocodeLocation(location);

  const url = new URL("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast");
  url.searchParams.set("latitude", String(place.latitude));
  url.searchParams.set("longitude", String(place.longitude));

  const response = await fetch(url);
```

```ts
interface TripFields {
  destination?: string;
  start_date?: string;

function getTrip(): TripRow {
  return db.prepare("SELECT * FROM trip WHERE id = 1").get() as TripRow;

export function getTripWithDays() {
  const days = db.prepare("SELECT * FROM trip_days ORDER BY day_number ASC").all() as TripDayRow[];
  return { ...getTrip(), days: days.map(tripDayToJson) };

export function updateTripPlan(fields: TripFields) {
  const updates: string[] = [];
  const values: unknown[] = [];

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(fields)) {
    if (value !== undefined) {
      updates.push(`${key} = ?`);
      values.push(value);
    }

  if (updates.length === 0) {
    return getTrip();

  updates.push("updated_at = datetime('now')");
  db.prepare(`UPDATE trip SET ${updates.join(", ")} WHERE id = 1`).run(...values);

      db.prepare(`UPDATE trip_days SET ${updates.join(", ")} WHERE id = ?`).run(...values, existing.id);
    }
    id = existing.id;
  } else {
    const result = db
      .prepare("INSERT INTO trip_days (day_number, date, summary, activities_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)")
      .run(dayNumber, fields.date ?? null, fields.summary ?? null, activitiesJson ?? null);
    id = Number(result.lastInsertRowid);
  }

  return db.prepare("SELECT * FROM trip_days WHERE id = ?").get(id);
```

**Shared no-auth-REST-API pattern** (there is no shared helper module â€” the pattern is duplicated by convention, not by code reuse):
- Build the URL with `new URL(base)` + `url.searchParams.set(...)` (never manual string concatenation/template literals for query strings).
- `const response = await fetch(url);` â€” no headers, no options object, no API key.
- `if (!response.ok) throw new Error("<Human description> failed (${response.status})");` â€” the message is `"<X> lookup failed"` / `"<X> failed"` pattern, always includes the numeric status in parens.
- `const data = (await response.json()) as <InlineOrNamedResponseType>;` â€” response typed via a local `interface` (Frankfurter) or an inline type literal with optional fields (Open-Meteo), not a full schema library â€” no zod/io-ts validation anywhere in this codebase.
- A second `if (missing-field) throw new Error("<specific, human-readable message>")` for "the API responded 200 but didn't have the data I need" cases (`No exchange rate found for X to Y`, `Could not find a location matching "X"`, `Weather service did not return current conditions`).
- The function returns a small, flat, LLM-friendly plain object with **renamed, lower_snake_case-with-units keys** (`temperature_celsius`, `wind_speed_kmh`, `converted`, `rate`) rather than passing the raw external response through â€” always reshape/rename before returning.
- No retries, no timeouts, no caching anywhere.
- Multi-step external calls (weather) use a private, unexported helper function (`geocodeLocation`) that the public exported tool function calls internally â€” see point 4 below.

## 4. Geocoding helper â€” exact precedent for "resolve fuzzy text into structured external-API input"

Confirmed: yes, it's a separate, **file-private, non-tool, non-exported** async helper inside `weather.ts`, called by `getCurrentWeather` before it does the "real" fetch. Exact signature and body (also shown above):

```ts
interface GeocodeResult {
  name: string;
  country?: string;
  latitude: number;
  longitude: number;
}

async function geocodeLocation(query: string): Promise<GeocodeResult> {
  const url = new URL("https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search");
  url.searchParams.set("name", query);
  url.searchParams.set("count", "1");

  const response = await fetch(url);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Geocoding failed (${response.status})`);
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { results?: GeocodeResult[] };
  const result = data.results?.[0];
  if (!result) {
    throw new Error(`Could not find a location matching "${query}"`);
  }
  return result;
}
```

Pattern to replicate for country-name â†’ ISO country-code resolution:
- Not a separate `TOOLS` entry, not exported, no schema of its own â€” it's plumbing invisible to the LLM and to `agent.ts`.
- Lives in the same file as (and directly above) the tool function that needs it.
- Takes the raw string the LLM supplied as the tool argument (`query`), hits a public no-auth API, takes only the first/best result (`count=1` / `[0]`), and throws a `Could not find a location matching "${query}"`-style error if nothing comes back â€” no fuzzy-match confirmation loop back to the LLM, no retry with alternate spellings.
- The public tool function (`getCurrentWeather`) awaits this helper first, then uses its structured output (`latitude`/`longitude`) to build the second, "real" API call.
